SAND2026-16518R Scaling Spectroradiometric Monitoring to an Algal Factory Farm Thomas A. Reichardt, Christopher Katinas, Jerilyn A. Timlin* January 2026 *Corresponding author, jatimli@sandia.gov Sandia National Laboratories is a multimission laboratory managed and operated by National Technology and Engineering Solutions of Sandia, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Honeywell International Inc., for the U.S. Department of Energy’s National Nuclear Security Administration under contract DE-NA0003525. 2 ABSTRACT This report briefly summarizes the spectroradiometric approach adapted and deployed as part of Task 4.2 within the BETO-funded Development of Integrated Screening, Cultivar Optimization, and Verification Research (DISCOVR) project, specifically task 4, “Increase crop protection and culture stability.” The goals of this subtask were to monitor ponds cultivating a variety of DISCOVR strains at the Arizona Center for Algae Technology and Innovation (AzCATI) with spectroradiometric technology to: • Predict biomass concentrations with high temporal frequency. • Optimize automated analysis methods that enabled feedback for pond automation strategies • Identify pond crash indicators from primary (pest/predator) and indirect (change in algal host) spectroscopic signals with potential for early treatment/intervention • Provide recommendations for technology deployment at scale. This report fulfills the deliverable requirement for the final bullet “provide recommendations for technology deployment at scale”. 3 ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS The authors gratefully acknowledge the following undergraduate interns who performed various tasks that enabled the research and development presented in this report (in no particular order): Ryan Henry (laboratory hyperspectral image data collection), Brandon Zabriskie (laboratory hyperspectral image data collection and analysis), Hayden Barolette (hyperspectral image analysis), Marina Holder (sensor maintenance and data collection at AzCATI, spectral analysis) and Isadora Gascho (sensor maintenance and data collection at AzCATI, spectral analysis). The authors wish to sincerely thank Dr. John McGowen and the entire AzCATI team for hosting the spectroradiometric monitoring platform at the AzCATI site and for partnering with the spectroradiometric team at Sandia to further the technology.
